## Phase 1 RCA — two independent, confirmed root causes (parsimony: each symptom needs its own)

**Worktree:** off `origin/main` @ `a3cb2de` (current). Step 0: no duplicate bug (only the ops-ledger session_log references this); reported-against floor `5c28ce6`.

### Root cause #1 — Windows collection blackout: 4 unguarded module-top `import fcntl`
`fcntl` is POSIX-only. The codebase has an **established portability-guard invariant** — 6 modules already do `try: import fcntl except ImportError: fcntl = None` with documented rationale ("absent on some platforms (e.g. plain Windows)") and `if fcntl is not None:` mkdir fallbacks (`_snapshot/janitor.py:363`, `rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py:55`, `git_fetch.py`, `repo_snapshot.py`). Four modules **violate** it with an *unconditional* module-top import:
- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py:62`, `src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py:45`, `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:5`, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py:69`.

**Mechanism (runtime-proven):** with `fcntl` unavailable, `import rebar` fails **entirely** — chain `rebar/__init__.py:46 → _lib_gates.py:19 → _lib_writes.py:26 → _commands/__init__.py:22 → doctor.py:52 → doctor_locks.py:69 (import fcntl)`. Because `import rebar` itself dies, **every** test module that imports rebar errors at collection → "collection error, many test modules." Simulating a non-POSIX platform (`sys.modules['fcntl']=None`) reproduces `ModuleNotFoundError`/`ImportError` for each of the 4 leaves in isolated subprocesses; the 6 guarded modules survive on their own and only fail *transitively* through these 4.

### Root cause #2 — py3.14 `sweep` red: over-broad socket guard blocks multiprocessing `forkserver` local IPC
The reporter's "unmocked network call" is a **misdiagnosis** — there is no network call. The failing test `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` starts a `multiprocessing.Process`. The autouse network guard (`tests/conftest.py:325`) patches `socket.socket.connect` for **all** address families. Python **3.14 changed the Linux default multiprocessing start method from `fork` to `forkserver`**, and `forkserver` connects to its server process over an **AF_UNIX** socket (local IPC) — which the guard intercepts and rejects with `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden…`.

**Discriminating experiment (runtime-proven, macOS):** under the guard, `fork` → child starts OK; `forkserver` → **BLOCKED with the exact ticket error**; `spawn` → OK. This isolates the cause to the **start method**, not py3.14 per se, and explains the symptom precisely: core tiers green (ubuntu py≤3.13 = `fork`; macOS = `spawn`), only py3.14+ Linux red (`forkserver`). Corroboration: `tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:50` already carries `@pytest.mark.allow_network` with the comment "subprocess pytest may touch **local** sockets" — prior friction from the same over-broad guard.

### Legitimacy (per-problem; resolved before Phase 2)
- **#2 = `defect`.** `test.yml:292` marks the py3.14 cell `experimental: false, locked: true` — "The 3.14 STABLE cell is a real signal." py3.14 green is a **must-pass design invariant**; the test fails it. Fix: narrow the guard to block only `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` (real network), allow AF_UNIX local IPC. Verified: forkserver IPC allowed, real TCP still blocked.
- **#1 = `defect` (portability-guard invariant).** Windows is "not a declared support target" (`test.yml:331`) and the leg is `continue-on-error`, **but** the job's documented purpose ("sweep Windows so a file-lock regression surfaces") is *defeated* by a total collection blackout, and the 4 unguarded imports violate the codebase's own established guard invariant. Fix scope = **collectability only** (guard the 4 imports to match the 6 siblings); making fcntl *locking* work on Windows is explicitly out of scope (non-support-target). Zero behavior change on any supported (POSIX) platform — `fcntl` stays the real module there.

### Attribution (`caused_by`)
Both red tiers were introduced by **one** commit: `7024c35` "ci: extend periodic sweep with breadth coverage" (**`13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43`**, 2026-08-26) added *both* the py3.14 "must-pass" cell **and** the Windows tier, without the portability work either requires (fcntl import guards; a forkserver-safe network guard). This is the obligation origin a reviewer could plausibly have caught. Deeper latent origins (noted, diverging from naive per-file blame): the over-broad socket guard predates trailers (extraction commit `b534f47`, 2026-06-08); the 4 unguarded fcntl imports span 4 commits — notably `git_locking.py` (`9e0a979b`, 2026-08-28) added its unguarded import *after* the Windows obligation existed. Recommended close: `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43`.

Proceeding to Phase 2 (RED→GREEN, held-out oracle, mutation teeth) + Step 7 class review (structural guard — the class earns one; `git_locking` re-entry is the located re-entry-past-review evidence).

## Phase 2 complete — fix pushed to Gerrit (NOT submitted/closed; orchestrator lands it)

**Gerrit change: [2463](https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2463)** — commit `80777cb` (`rebar-ticket:` trailer + DCO sign-off + Change-Id `Idbc8dc1`). Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`.

### Proven root causes (two independent, per parsimony)
**RC#1 — Windows collection blackout (defect).** `fcntl` is POSIX-only. Four modules did an *unconditional* module-top `import fcntl`: `_store/lock.py`, `_store/git_locking.py`, `reducer/marker.py`, `_commands/doctor_locks.py`. `import rebar` transitively reaches `doctor_locks.py`, so the ENTIRE package failed to collect off POSIX → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` on the sweep-windows tier. Runtime-proven via `sys.modules['fcntl']=None` (simulated absent module). The codebase already establishes the guard invariant in **three** legitimate shapes — module-top `try/except ImportError→None` (janitor/repo_snapshot/git_fetch), an `if sys.platform != "win32"` conditional (`alert_store.py`), and function-local lazy imports (`recent_creates.py`, `hlc.py`). Fix = guard the four with the try/except shape (collectability only; Windows *locking* out of scope — not a declared support target; on non-POSIX `fcntl=None` so a lock call would `AttributeError`, which is acceptable). POSIX unchanged.

**RC#2 — py3.14 network-forbidden (defect); reporter's "unmocked network call" was a misdiagnosis.** The autouse `_network_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`) patched `socket.socket.connect` for ALL address families. Python 3.14 changed the Linux default multiprocessing start method `fork`→`forkserver`; forkserver reaches its server over an **AF_UNIX** socket (local IPC, never network), which the all-families guard rejected → the exact `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden`. Discriminating experiment (forced start methods): fork/spawn=OK, forkserver=BLOCKED. Fix = narrow the `connect` seam to AF_INET/AF_INET6 only, delegating other families to the captured real connect; the `create_connection` seam (real-TCP-only) is unchanged.

### RED→GREEN (held out, mutation-checked)
- `tests/unit/test_fcntl_import_guard.py` — 4 modules + `import rebar` import under a simulated fcntl-less interpreter (subprocess); + AST-gate discrimination (true-positive, a true-negative for each of the three guarded shapes, sanction). Mutation: unwrapping `doctor_locks` → exact `ModuleNotFoundError: import of fcntl halted` RED; restored.
- `tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py` — AF_UNIX connect + a forkserver `Process` start under the guard (GREEN), real AF_INET connect still blocked (teeth). Mutation: reverting the guard to all-families → both RED with the guard RuntimeError; restored.
- **Original-report replication:** `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` under forced `forkserver` → RED (exact ticket error) pre-fix, GREEN post-fix.

### Structural guard (class earns a gate)
`scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` — stdlib-only AST scan over `src/rebar`, flags an *unconditional* module-top `import fcntl`, credits try/except **and** `if` (platform) guards **and** function-local imports, with a `# fcntl-guard-ok:` sanction. Wired into `make lint`. Portable: no CI provider required (project.portability). Two `import fcntl` test siblings (`test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py`, `test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py`) now `pytest.importorskip("fcntl")`.

### Validation
`make lint` ✅, `make typecheck` ✅ (720 files). Parity sweep over the change blast radius (`-k network/socket/fcntl/lock/marker/multiprocess/forkserver/guard/…` across `tests/unit`): **1614 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed**. Plan-review gate: **certified** (PASS after description corrections).

### Attribution / recommended close
`caused_by` → **13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43** (commit `7024c35`, "ci: extend periodic sweep with breadth coverage") added BOTH the py3.14 must-pass cell and the Windows tier without the portability work. Recommended close: **`--class=plan_defect --caused-by=13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43`**.

### For the orchestrator
No design/behavior escalation needed. Implemented directly (fix is mechanism-dictated/mechanical) while preserving strict RED→GREEN + per-defect mutation check + refactor-litmus. **Do not close until change 2463 is `Verified +1`** (green CI is not substitutable by the completion-verifier).

## Surface
GitHub Actions, repo navapbc/rebar, workflow **Test Suite (mirror)** (scheduled/dispatch, non-blocking mirror tier), matrix `sweep (…)` jobs. Blocking core tiers pass on main; only the experimental `sweep` matrix is red.

## Signatures (two distinct sub-failures)
1. **sweep (windows)** — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` at collection; Windows tier cannot collect.
2. **sweep (py3.14)** — `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py::test_a_contended_fcntl_leg_reads_as_held` fails `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests`.

(The `sweep (macos, full suite)` / `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` legs are the recurrence of closed `e3e0-2e7c-b280-4b4a`, tracked there — not this ticket.)

## Severity: P3
Mirror/experimental tier — non-blocking. CI-hygiene / cross-platform-portability signal.

---

## Fix plan (Phase 2) — two independent root causes, confirmed in Phase 1 RCA comment

**RC#1 (Windows collection blackout):** 4 modules do an *unconditional* module-top `import fcntl` — `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`, `src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py`. Because `import rebar` transitively hits `doctor_locks.py`, ALL collection dies on non-POSIX. The codebase already establishes that a module-top fcntl import must be made *conditional*, and does so with **three distinct legitimate shapes** (none is a single uniform pattern):
  - **module-top `try/except ImportError → fcntl = None`** — `_snapshot/janitor.py`, `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, `_snapshot/git_fetch.py`, `rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py`'s sibling guarded modules;
  - **`if sys.platform != "win32": import fcntl` / `else: fcntl = None`** — `_engine/rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py:12-15`;
  - **function-local (lazy) `import fcntl`** — `_commands/recent_creates.py:64` (inside `_journal_lock`), `_store/hlc.py:106` (inside `_hlc_lock`); a deferred import never runs at collection time, so it never breaks collection.

Fix = guard the 4 unconditional imports with the module-top `try/except ImportError → None` shape (collectability only; Windows fcntl *locking* is out of scope — non-support-target). On non-POSIX, `fcntl` binds to `None`, so a subsequent `fcntl.flock(...)` call site inside those 4 modules would raise `AttributeError` at call time — that is acceptable and in-scope-excluded: Windows is not a declared support target and these are POSIX-only lock paths; the deliverable is import/collection success, not Windows locking. Zero behavior change on POSIX (fcntl stays the real module).

**RC#2 (py3.14 red):** the autouse `_network_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`) patches **two** seams: `patch.object(socket.socket, "connect", _guard_socket_connect)` AND `patch("socket.create_connection", side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`. The `connect` seam rejected **all** address families; py3.14's Linux default start-method change `fork`→`forkserver` makes `multiprocessing` reach its server over an **AF_UNIX** (local IPC) connect, which the all-families guard wrongly rejects. Fix = narrow the **`connect`** seam only: block just `AF_INET`/`AF_INET6` (real network) and delegate every other family (AF_UNIX etc.) to the captured original `socket.socket.connect`. The **`create_connection`** seam is left AS-IS — it is a real-TCP-only helper (always builds an AF_INET/AF_INET6 socket), so it needs no family check and blocking it wholesale stays correct.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` — `import fcntl` guarded (module-top `try/except ImportError → None`); POSIX behavior unchanged.
- [x] `src/rebar/_store/git_locking.py` — `import fcntl` guarded.
- [x] `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py` — `import fcntl` guarded.
- [x] `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` — `import fcntl` guarded (the leaf that breaks `import rebar`).
- [x] RED→GREEN: the 4 modules import under simulated non-POSIX (`sys.modules['fcntl']=None`) and `import rebar` succeeds — proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_fcntl_import_guard.py`.
- [x] Structural guard `scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` (AST; stdlib-only, wired into `make lint`) fails only on a genuinely **unconditional** module-top `import fcntl` in `src/rebar`. It treats an import as guarded when it is (a) inside a `try`, (b) inside an `if`/`else` (the `sys.platform` conditional), OR (c) function-local (never module-top). A `# fcntl-guard-ok: <reason>` marker is the sanctioned escape hatch. Ships true-positive + true-negative (one case for EACH of the three live shapes — try/except like `git_fetch.py`, `sys.platform` like `alert_store.py`, function-local like `hlc.py`) + refactor-survival tests — proven by `python scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` and its test.
- [x] Step7 test siblings `tests/unit/test_fetch_common_dir_coordination.py` and `tests/unit/test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py` use `pytest.importorskip("fcntl")` so they skip (not error) on non-POSIX.
- [x] `tests/conftest.py` — the `connect` seam blocks only AF_INET/AF_INET6 and delegates other families to the real connect; the `create_connection` seam is unchanged — proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py`.
- [x] RED→GREEN: a `forkserver` `multiprocessing.Process` starts under the guard; an AF_UNIX connect is allowed; a real AF_INET connect is still blocked (teeth).

## Testing
- `python scripts/check_fcntl_import_guard.py` — the new structural guard (also via `make lint`).
- `pytest tests/unit/test_fcntl_import_guard.py tests/unit/test_network_guard_local_ipc.py` — the two RED→GREEN regressions.
- `pytest tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor_locks.py` — original-report replication (under forkserver).
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — clean.

### Portability (project.portability)
The structural guard is a stdlib-only AST script wired into `make lint` — no CI provider required, runnable locally and under any CI. The network-guard narrowing is interpreter/OS-agnostic (a socket-family check).

## Provenance
Periodic ops-error sweep. `caused_by` → `13ad-4c6f-4074-4f43` (added both red tiers). See Phase 1 RCA comment for full mechanism proofs + attribution.
